The speed of light in vacuum is a universal physical constant denoted c, exactly equal to 299792458 m⋅s−1.
It is exact because, by international agreement, a metre is defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1⁄299792458 second.
The value 299,792,458 metres per second is approximately 1 billion kilometres per hour; 700 million miles per hour.
